title: Laguerre central limit for nontrivial admissible finite-second-moment BC_q Jacobi walks with d=1,2,4 and p in {q,...,2q-1} or p>2q-1
author: Margit Rosler; Michael Voit
source_title: A Central Limit Theorem for Random Walks on the Dual of a Compact Grassmannian
difficulty_reason: The limit theorem requires a uniform quantitative Mehler-Heine comparison between Heckman-Opdam Jacobi polynomials and matrix Bessel functions. The proof also develops positive quadratic moment functions and tightness for convolution walks, then transfers characteristic-transform convergence to the Laguerre density, including admissible walks where general product-linearization positivity is not presumed.
source_version: Official SIGMA 11 (2015) article 013, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2015.013; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Complete Theorem3.12 and all local quantitative Mehler-Heine, moment growth, differentiability, variance-additivity and tightness proofs read. Admissible probability measures are supported on weights for which every product-linearization coefficient against every other weight is nonnegative; general positivity for noninteger p is not assumed. The geometric singular-measure cases use the explicitly defined Haar pushforward in Remark2.3 and the same compact-domain estimates, an author-described routine adaptation. Limit normalization is S_n/sqrt(n sigma-squared), with sigma-squared=sum m(lambda)nu(lambda)>0. The Laguerre density and its Bessel transform are stated in Section3.3. No tensor-power corollary, rank-one specialization or law of large numbers is counted.

statement_scope: Full Theorem3.12: q>=1, d in{1,2,4}, p in{q,q+1,...,2q-1} union(2q-1,infinity); an admissible probability measure nu on P-plus, nu!=delta-zero and sum lambda1-squared nu finite. The Jacobi-convolution Markov walk started at0, divided by sqrt(n sigma-squared), converges weakly on the ordered positive Weyl chamber to the stated Laguerre density. No arbitrary non-admissible measure or other multiplicity range claimed.
editorial_warning: Remark2.3 ends with a range upper endpoint2p-1 while its opening and Theorem2.4 state2q-1; equation(3.3) repeats lambda1 where the Gaussian transform uses all q coordinates. The selected theorem range and complete transform limit(3.7) explicitly specify the scope and limiting quadratic form. Original pages remain unchanged. The rescaled Mehler–Heine display in the final proof is reproduced exactly as printed, together with the full preceding quantitative estimate and all scaling definitions; no source formula is repaired.
